summary:
FOUR OF THE FIVE REFUSALS DO WHAT IS CLAIMED. THE FIFTH IS A DEAD GUARD WHOSE OWN FILE NOW STATES THREE THINGS THAT ARE FALSE AT HEAD, AND THE OWNER'S SECOND SENTENCE DOES NOT REACH IT AT ALL.

METHOD. The work is committed as 40d2446; the pre-change tree is f11ae02. I materialised BOTH with `git archive` outside the repository and re-ran the whole 60-cell matrix myself in 60 fresh processes per tree (5 accessors x 6 values x 2 switch positions), plus the CKPT Gate rendered at 24 further points (6 values x 2 switch positions x CKPT_DIR set/unset). I did not edit any file in src/, tests/ or docs/.

WHAT I CONFIRM. EVAL.curve_period, DOM.manage_period and MEM.rekey_period each refuse -1000, -5 and -1 with a LeverError naming the lever and the value, fire before U.Windows is constructed, leave 0/1/200 byte-identical to f11ae02, and revert exactly to f11ae02 behaviour with their switch False. CKPT.save_period's refusal is intact and its Gate prints no false equation at any of the 24 points I rendered. The assigned eval citation fix is real: `sed -n '137,138p'` on f11ae02's src/eval/api.py reads exactly "A period accessor is one / construction over one declared lever", and HEAD reads "over ITS DECLARED LEVERS" with save_period's two levers named. The unfiled DOM citation defect is real and is exactly as described: f11ae02 src/domains/api.py:444 reads `Cadences.due('dom.manage', FAB.manage_every, clock)` and HEAD:476 reads `DOM.manage_every`, while fabric/api.py:2467 still correctly reads `Cadences.due('fab.manage', FAB.manage_every, clock)`. Every one of the 25 `path.py::symbol` citations added across the five files resolves to a real symbol. ASSEMBLY_ORDER is 39 rows with CAP.startup_refusals at 29 and `cadence` at 35; MEM.maintain is LOOP_ORDER row 26, DOM.manage row 5, FAB.manage row 7 -- so the accessor really does precede every second reader. RUN, WORLD and CAP are the only three `def startup_refusals` in src/. No wire spent, no lever declared, no signature moved, nothing stubbed.

THE REFUTATION, AND IT IS THE HEADLINE. src/fabric/api.py::manage_period's refusal IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH EVERY PRODUCTION PATH, and the file says the opposite three times in present tense. A sibling agent's change to spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows landed IN THE SAME COMMIT and now raises UnitError on a negative period_windows -- inside the `OPT.batch_windows -> FAB.d_manage_period` coupling compute, i.e. at spine/assemble.py:1426, BEFORE any Config exists. Measured: `assemble.build(environ={'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY':'-5'})` raises `spine.units.UnitError` out of src/spine/derive.py:356; `compose(environ={'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY':'-5'})` ends there too, NOT at CAP.startup_refusals like the other four. So the filed repro -- "build() still succeeds, so that wire exists in the ledger whatever this accessor later does" -- does not reproduce, and the report's "Verified in fresh processes for all five negatives; every one ended at CAP.startup_refusals" is true for four, false for the fifth. Three sentences shipped inside src/fabric/api.py are false at HEAD: (i) "`assemble.build` accepts FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5 and freezes it" under a heading reading WHAT A NEGATIVE ACTUALLY DOES TODAY; (ii) "that function FLOORS AT ONE FLUSH"; (iii) "the floored Flushes(1) still exists in the ledger". The tree already knows: tests/test_fabric.py::F8 prints "so FAB's own guard is UNREACHABLE through assemble.build today" and docs/04_CONTRACT.md:897-903 records it. Only the owning file does not.

AND THE OWNER'S SECOND SENTENCE DOES NOT REACH FAB. I set `fabric.api.REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD = False` and rebuilt: still `UnitError`. FAB's switch is INERT IN BOTH POSITIONS through assemble.build, so "if it has a bad effect, we can turn off the refusal" cannot be exercised for FAB_MANAGE_EVERY by flipping FAB's switch. That is not a defect the four siblings share, and nothing in f_periods' report says it.

TWO NUMERIC CLAIMS IN THE REPORT ARE WRONG AGAINST THE TREE THEY SHIPPED INTO. "With the switch True all 15 negative cells raise LeverError" -- I measure 12; FAB's three raise UnitError from build and never reach the accessor. "With the switch False all 30 cells are byte-identical to the pre-change tree" -- I measure 24 of 30. CKPT's three negative cells differ because f11ae02 refused them UNCONDITIONALLY (that is the intended effect of bringing CKPT under the switch, but it is not byte-identity), and FAB's three differ because the assembly now refuses. The 15 non-negative cells ARE byte-identical, exactly as claimed.

THE OFF POSITION IS NOT "SAFE", IT IS ARITHMETICALLY HONEST AND SEMANTICALLY FALSE. I rendered the CKPT Gate at every reachable point. The f-string does what is claimed: at CKPT_EVERY=-5, CKPT_DIR=runs/x, switch False the line reads "armed, did not fire (-5 vs 1) -- CKPT_EVERY=-5 with CKPT_DIR set: ...", value and equation agreeing. But the REASON that follows is "the only saves this run makes are the FINAL one and any SIGUSR1" -- and the same file argues at length, correctly, that a negative under Cadences.due's elapsed-since-last-fire contract is a checkpoint written EVERY window. So the OFF configuration prints a sentence asserting the exact opposite of what the file says the value does. The previous round fixed the false EQUATION; the false CLAIM is still there and the switch is what makes it reachable again.

TWO OF THE FOUR FILED `unfinished` ITEMS WERE ALREADY DISCHARGED BY SIBLINGS IN THE SAME COMMIT: spine/assemble.py no longer floors a negative FAB_MANAGE_EVERY (derive refuses it), and docs/04_CONTRACT.md:884-910 records the ruling in full, including FAB's unreachability. The other two hold: train/api.py:78 "EVAL.curve_period and its three siblings" is off by one, and MEM.probe_every has no accessor to refuse in.

ZERO TESTS EXERCISE FOUR OF THE FIVE REFUSALS. `grep -rn "DOM_MANAGE_EVERY\|EVAL_CURVE_EVERY\|MEM_REKEY_EVERY" tests/*.py` returns NOTHING, and no test sets CKPT_EVERY negative. Only FAB's is covered, by tests/test_fabric.py::F8 -- and that check reports it is standing over the ASSEMBLY's refusal, not FAB's. Flipping any of the four switches to False, or deleting any of the four guards, fails nothing in the suite.

SUITE, RUN BY ME, REAL NUMBERS: ownership 13 checks + 32 self-test cases 0 failing; contract 15 + 59, 0; census 8 + self-test, 0; assemble 9, 0; couplings 4, 0; derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches; and tests/test_fabric.py 8 checks 0 failing. The report's suite_after says "IDENTICAL TO THE BASELINE" quoting ownership 13+27, contract 15+54 and census 7 -- those are not the tree's numbers now, because siblings added cases in the same commit.
